# Mesh and scene fixtures

Authored examples are generated by `examples/fixtures/mesh_scene.rs` and are MIT licensed with Catwalk. Native containers use their actual binary encoding. The authored production-3MF examples exercise package-local references, colliding object IDs, nested local transforms, per-part materials, ignored child builds and mixed units. The OBJ/PLY wireframes contain actual polyline/edge geometry.

`draco-google-cube.drc` and compressed glTF/GLB copies retain Google's Apache-2.0 `cube_att.obj.edgebreaker.cl4.2.2.drc` testdata, from https://github.com/google/draco/tree/main/testdata. The original license is `GOOGLE-DRACO-LICENSE`.

## Independently exported 3MF packages

These packages are unmodified upstream resources, renamed only for the corpus. They are separate test assets distributed under their upstream repositories' GNU Affero General Public License version 3; Catwalk's MIT license applies to its code and authored fixtures. Each repository's complete original license is retained below. Regeneration copies the checked-in bytes and requires no slicer executable or network. Previews render the decoded model geometry rather than an embedded preview image.

Upstream package metadata is retained verbatim. The Bambu/Orca packages contain production-extension paths; this is real slicer output, distinct from the clearly labeled authored XML regression packages. Public producer provenance is recorded at exact source commits. These representative files do not establish compatibility with every slicer version, project extension or material type.

All referenced corpus resources remain inside this directory. Regeneration uses Rust and retained fixture bytes, without external executables or native codecs.
